messages.author: 4b880dbd85e89f08
messages.subject: Arrange
parts:
Hi all,

I noticed that arrange seems to drop rownames.

rownames(arrange(mtcars, cyl, desc(disp)))

gives different rownames than rownames(mtcars). I think it would be
nice if we could preserve the original rownames. Here is my hack.

# --
rows_original <- rownames(mtcars)
mtcars$index <- 1:nrow(mtcars)
mtcars2 <- arrange(mtcars, cyl, desc(disp))
rownames(mtcars2) <- rows_original[mtcars2$index]

# clean up
drop_c <- colnames(mtcars2) %in% "index"
mtcars2 <- mtcars2[,!drop_c]
rm(drop_c, rows_original)

# --

Anirban

hi,

probably this is a simple hack

arrange2 <- function(df, ...) df[eval(substitute(order(...)), df,
parent.frame()),]

so, should arrange be like this?

arrange <- function (df, ..., drop.rowname = TRUE) {
ord <- eval(substitute(order(...)), df, parent.frame())
if (drow.rowname) unrowname(df[ord, ])
else df[ord, ]
}

messages.subject: Re: Arrange
parts: > I noticed that arrange seems to drop rownames.

Yes, pretty much everything in plyr ignores rownames, mainly because I
don't think they're very useful. The restriction for uniqueness is to
strong, and ends up being a nuisance in most circumstances. I'd
recommend moving your rownames to a real column, and the forgetting
about rownames altogether.
